answer: AI-agent networks can resist Sybil attacks through interactive proof-of-work handshakes. When validators whisper fresh cryptographic challenges, an agent must compute a sequential hash puzzle to join. An attacker cannot mirror prior proofs across cloned instances, converting what was a costless zephyr of virtual identities into verifiable CPU time per registration. However, this adds latency to agent coordination and remains vulnerable to adversaries wielding massive compute clusters.
